key_insight: Causal discovery links steel composition, sheet thickness, and electrode tip diameter to distinct resistance spot-welding signal features, improving physical interpretability beyond correlation alone.
engineering_relevance: These relationships can inform interpretable weld monitoring and process adjustment across heterogeneous material stacks and electrode configurations.
method: Apply a two-phase causal discovery framework to multicollinear stack-up configurations.
Cluster time series to characterize process-signal morphology.
Analyze how material and geometric factors relate to resistance, displacement, and force signals.
evidence_signal: Analysis of 15,096 representative profiles derived from over 1.8 million welds found that reducing tip face diameter from 8 to 6 mm increased the initial resistance peak by 9%.
watch_item: Discovered dependencies do not by themselves establish that process adjustments will improve weld quality; intervention-based validation remains important.
paper_title: Causal discovery of signal morphology drivers in steel resistance spot welding: a high-dimensional data analysis
